business: Andrea Beauty House — a beauty salon in New City, Podgorica, running three rooms under one roof (adult salon, a braids studio, and a separate kids space), each with its own Instagram profile. Route: src/app/(me)/demo/andrea-beauty-house/
artDirection: A warm "house" built on one repeated shape: an arch (`rounded-t-[50%]`) lifted from the salon's real pink phone booth, applied to every photo, doorway and detail. Palette is warm white → blush → a peach "kids field" → a single full-bleed berry closing panel, with gold reserved for hairlines; Fraunces display serif (berry italics used as a voice) sits over Work Sans body. Photography-led throughout, with one drawn three-strand braid mark standing in for the one room that has no public photograph.
strengths: The arch motif is genuinely subject-grounded, not decorative: it is the shape of the salon's own pink phone booth, and it is stated once as `archMat`/`archPhoto` (page.tsx L55-56) and reused as doorway, room, and detail. This is the page's signature element and must survive.
The pink-booth hero photograph is a real, specific, memorable asset — no other salon site in Montenegro opens on that image. Keep it as the hero.

Content honesty is exemplary and rare: `researchOnly` in data.ts withholds conflicting phones, hours, addresses and prices instead of inventing them, and there are zero fake stats, testimonials, badges or 'trusted by' filler. Keep this discipline.
The three-doors concept is true to how the business actually operates (three real Instagram profiles) — the idea itself is strong and specific.

Palette is disciplined and documented with real contrast ratios in andrea.module.css (L15-32); berry is genuinely rationed to doors/CTAs plus one full-bleed closing panel, which gives the page a single loud colour moment.
Fraunces + Work Sans is the right pairing for this brand — soft-serif warmth without tipping into a children's page — and latin-ext subsetting is correct for č/ć/š/ž/đ.
The `knock` micro-interaction (andrea.module.css L34-58) is one idea, runs once, and is reduced-motion guarded. Conceptually perfect for a page about doors.

FloatingDoor.tsx is unusually well-reasoned: it stays off until the hero CTA leaves, steps aside at the closing section, rAF-throttled rect reads (with the documented reason for not using IntersectionObserver), and correct `aria-hidden`/`tabIndex` handling.
DemoPhoto usage is correct throughout — explicit width/height, per-instance `sizes`, priority only on the hero, and descriptive Serbian alt text on every frame.

issues.issue: The `#closing-sentinel` div is the FIRST CHILD of the `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-[1.1fr_0.9fr]` container, so it consumes grid cell 1. The result on desktop: 'Vrata su otvorena.' is shoved into the right column, the entire top-left quadrant of the berry panel is empty maroon (~600×250px of nothing), and the address block wraps onto a second row bottom-left. The page's final, most important moment renders as a broken layout. Verified in the 1440px screenshot.

issues.issue: Photos sit inside their blush mats inconsistently: the left macaron arch shows ~55px of bare blush shelf below the image, the right one ~15px, the salon thumbnail shows an L-shaped blush strip right and below. Cause is twofold — `archPhoto` hard-codes `h-full` while every call site also passes `h-24`/`h-56`/`h-72`/`h-80` (conflicting height utilities whose winner depends on stylesheet order), and `DemoPhoto` returns a bare inline `<picture>` so the mat gets line-box descender space. The result looks like a rendering bug, not a mat.

The single channel is Instagram DM, repeated nine times (header, hero, three door cards, kids, braids, closing, sticky). data.ts documents this as deliberate pending owner confirmation, which is defensible for an outreach concept, but as shipped the page's conversion path is one channel with no fallback and no urgency, and the salon section — the main business — is the only room section with no CTA at all.

verdict: The art direction is real and worth defending — the arch lifted from the salon's own pink phone booth is a genuine subject-grounded signature, the palette is disciplined, and the content is honest in a way most demo pages are not. But the execution has not caught up with the concept. One outright layout bug destroys the closing panel on desktop, the tablet hero renders both CTAs with wrapped labels, and the braids panel — meant to be a confident moment — reads as a placeholder. Underneath those, the page's best idea (three doors, three real profiles) is served as a uniform three-card grid, and the three sections that follow share one identical heading-paragraph-pill grammar, so the page's density never varies and its hierarchy is flat from the fold to the footer. It does not look like 500 other AI sites, but it does look like a strong concept rendered at about 70 percent: too much empty space in the lower half of every section, several photos placed at sizes or crops that defeat them, and one image used twice. Fix the three blockers, break the card grid, and give at least one section real depth, and this reaches the level the client is asking for.
